source_title: After 18-Month Investigation, Chairs DeFazio and Larsen Release Final Committee Report on Boeing 737 MAX
publisher_issuer: U.S. House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure
company_context: Boeing Company manufactured the 737 MAX, which entered commercial service in 2017 and suffered two fatal crashes within five months (Lion Air, October 2018; Ethiopian Airlines, March 2019). The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee conducted an 18-month investigation and issued a 238-page final report.
evidence_summary: The final committee report documents serious flaws in the design, development, and certification of the 737 MAX. Two crashes within five months killed 346 people (including eight Americans). The crashes were tied to the MCAS automated nose-down system reacting to faulty data from a single angle-of-attack sensor. Boeing withheld critical information from the FAA, customers, and pilots, including internal test data showing it took a Boeing test pilot more than 10 seconds to diagnose and respond to uncommanded MCAS activation — a condition the pilot described as 'catastrophic' — versus the federal assumption of a 4-second pilot response. The report concluded the crashes were the culmination of faulty technical assumptions, lack of management transparency, and grossly insufficient FAA oversight.
outcome_evidence: The 238-page final report (released 16 September 2020) attributes 346 deaths to design failures, Boeing's concealment of information, and grossly insufficient FAA oversight; the 737 MAX was grounded worldwide and Boeing incurred massive financial and reputational damage.
